wording: Shared factor (method): in all four topics the evidence is about reports or beliefs, not direct access to the object. Soul research measures beliefs about continuity after death; Spirit research measures reports of mystical experience; the Subconscious is inferred from awareness tests; and report demands themselves produce some 'markers' of consciousness.
limits: Each part is Established in its own ledger; grouping them as one factor is this report's judgment.

wording: Shared factor (method): all four topics classify people or states with cut-offs on noisy measures, and in each the track showed the cut-off misclassifies: NDE cases (Soul), 'complete' mystical experiences (Spirit), 'subliminal' stimuli (Subconscious) and negative covert-consciousness tests (Consciousness).
limits: The four results are simulations with illustrative inputs; they show how cut-offs behave, not the error rate of any real study.

wording: Shared factor (method): headline effects are fragile in all four topics. Mortality-salience and analytic-priming effects (Soul), induced-awe effects (Spirit) and behavioural priming (Subconscious) failed replication, and adversarial testing challenged predictions of both leading consciousness theories (Consciousness).
limits: For Consciousness the fragility is of theory predictions, not replication of an effect, so the factor is a family resemblance; hence Plausible.

wording: Shared factor (subject matter): death and the end of life join Soul (beliefs about what continues; end-of-life and near-death experiences), Spirit (death anxiety after psychedelic experiences) and Consciousness (possible awareness during circulatory arrest; existential suffering in disorders of consciousness). limits: TD-CONS-29 rests on 9 usable EEGs and 3 guesses (TD-CONS-30); the end-of-life evidence is thin.

wording: Shared factor (subject matter): sleep and dreaming appear in three ledgers: nearly half of end-of-life experiences occurred during sleep (Soul), dream sampling of reactivated memories and the Advaita account of dreaming and deep sleep (Subconscious), and anaesthesia dreaming as disconnected consciousness (Consciousness).

wording: Difference: each topic has a different empirical object. Soul: beliefs about a soul, not a soul. Spirit: reported self-transcendent experience, not the reality it reports. Subconscious: processing inferred from behaviour without report, in several distinct senses. Consciousness: experience and its neural correlates, with theories under adversarial test.
limits: Follows the SSSC FRAMEWORK boundaries; a judgment about scope, not a measured result.

wording: Difference: the Subconscious is the only one of the four defined by contrast with another of them. What counts as subconscious depends on where the conscious/unconscious boundary is drawn and on how awareness is measured, so Subconscious and Consciousness are a dependent pair, not two independent topics.
limits: Soul and Spirit are also often defined against each other in traditions; that is examined in x6 (main Reports 3 and 4).

wording: Traditions and history (descriptive): Yogacara posits a store consciousness described as 'a subliminal form of cognitive awareness', Advaita treats dreaming and deep sleep as states pointing to turiya, and Leibniz allowed infinitely many degrees of consciousness with unconscious 'petites perceptions'. Each describes the subliminal as a form or degree of consciousness rather than its opposite.
limits: Established as a description of what these sources report the traditions hold, not as true.

wording: Unity in a tradition (Philosophical/Spiritual): Advaita Vedanta joins three of the topics in one teaching, in which deep sleep (a state below waking awareness), turiya (pure consciousness) and the true self are aspects of one reality to be realised. This is a described teaching, not a demonstrated unity.
limits: One tradition among many; others (for example Yogacara's no-self view, x6) divide the topics differently.

limits: An absence of evidence in these ledgers, not evidence of absence; tested again in each cycle.
